overview.text: Apple Inc. is a technology company that began as Apple Computer Company, a partnership formed by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne on April 1, 1976; it became incorporated as Apple Computer, Inc. in 1977. Its early Apple II reached beyond computer hobbyists, and the spreadsheet program VisiCalc helped boost that model’s sales. In 1984, Apple introduced the Macintosh, a computer that helped make graphical, mouse-driven personal computing familiar to a wider public. Its later iPhone combined phone, music-player, and internet functions in one touch-controlled product. Apple now sells devices including Mac and iPhone and offers services such as the App Store, iCloud, and Apple Music, linking hardware, software, and online services.

key_facts.text: The Computer History Museum dates Apple’s founding to April 1, 1976, as a partnership of Jobs, Wozniak, and Wayne; Wayne withdrew 11 days later. Apple incorporated the following January.
The Apple II debuted in 1977 with color graphics and expansion slots, helping Apple reach beyond computer hobbyists.
VisiCalc, developed for the Apple II, automated spreadsheet calculations and helped boost the computer’s sales.
Apple introduced the Macintosh in 1984; the Computer History Museum describes it as helping bring graphical computing to more people.
Steve Jobs introduced the iPhone in 2007 as a touch-controlled combination of an iPod, a phone, and an internet communications device.
